page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; marginal notes in the right margin; catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: nis dominicę exponamus. Ac primò quidem cō-furrectionis[?]tra fanaticos quosdā spiritus, quib. volupe est, oia ea, quę de Christo vere dicuntur, inanib. spectris deludere, firmiter tenendum est, eum vere à mortuis resurrexisse, h.e, animā ipsius ad corpus, à quoVerè resur-rexit corpo-re, quod ca-ciderat. per inenarrabiles angustias, cruciatus & terrores avulsa fuerat, verè rediisse, illiq; unitā fuisse: atq; idem illud corpus, quod paulò ante à furiosis militib. indignis modis tractatum, ac flagris laceratum fuerat, quodq; vi mortis ceciderat, verè resurrexisse: id quod cum ex aliis, tum praecipuè ex his causis fit manifestum. Quod n. λόγῳ[?] naturalis æterni Dei filius ex definito patris sui consilio ad liberandum genus humanum semel assumsit, hoc nunquam ac ne in morte quidem deposuit, nec in æternum deponet: sed omnipotenti sua virtute in cœlum evexit: ac in extremo judicio omnibus hominibus reprobis simul & electis adspiciendum dabit: his in perpetuum gaudium & felicitatem: illis in æternum mœrorem & cruciatū. Quid? quod natura nostra justissimo & immoto judicio Dei propter peccata mori debuit, ac rursum è terra suscitari? Per hominem n. mors, inqt Apostolus, per hominem quoq; resurrectio. Quin & ipse Christus multoties prædixit, eundem Filium hominis moriturum & resurrecturum esse: Et angelus diserte verbis mulieribus fatetur, illum ipsum surrexisse, qui cum illis loquutus fuerat, cum adhuc in Galilæa esset: Surrexit, inquit, non est hic: præcedet vos in Galilæam. Quis igitur verbis ipsius CHRISTI fidem non habeat? Quis nisi summa cum animi obstinatione

page.notes: Page 551, Liber IV, with the number printed top right. Left-margin text cut off at the line start ("nis dominicę") is a fragment, kept as is. Uncertain readings: "furrectionis" in the right margin (the marginal word is hard to make out) and the Greek word "λόγῳ" (its final accent and letters are faint). The margin reference "1.Cor.15.21" beside the "Per hominem" line is in the right margin and is not transcribed as a note, because it is an ordinary printed reference. The printed "inqt" is an abbreviation of "inquit" and is kept as printed. The printed reference "1.Cor.15.21" is also kept as "1.Cor.15.21" in the note position. Catchword "angeli" and signature "Mm iiij." are at the foot right and left.
